title: Integration tests, migrations, and a release rehearsal
outcome: Prove the deployed configuration, database changes, and failure recovery beyond mock tests.
useCase: A service release with a schema change and background delivery.
drawbacks: Integration environments cost time and still do not cover every production condition.
cue: Test the boundary. Rehearse the release. Separate data recovery.

trace.title: Built artifact
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A unit suite can pass while the real application has the wrong bean, migration, permission, or SQL behavior. Keep focused integration tests for the boundaries you rely on.

Use a disposable real database when engine behavior matters.

A release changes code, configuration, and sometimes data. Old and new instances may overlap.

A migration should remain compatible during that overlap. A code rollback does not restore deleted data or unsend messages.

Rehearse a small release with a known failure. Observe readiness, startup migration ownership, graceful shutdown, in-flight requests, and a rollback decision.

A runbook is a short path from symptom to check to safe action to verification.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Build an immutable artifact → verify its configuration → apply a deliberate migration → start and check readiness → send a smoke request → observe → promote or roll back.

Keep migration execution separate from ordinary request scaling.

Tests should show both permitted and denied behavior, transaction rollback, and an adapter failure. A green health endpoint alone does not prove the feature works.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Tests wrapped in a transaction can hide after-commit behavior. A fake repository cannot prove a unique index.

A rollback button cannot undo every data effect.
